concepts.name: The Concept Of Human Right Human Rights
concepts.simple_definition: The concept of human right Human rights are basic to humanity
concepts.deep_explanation: They apply to all people everywhere
concepts.real_example: Practical example of The concept of human right Human rights  from page 134.
concepts.common_confusion: Students sometimes confuse The concept of human right Human rights  with adjacent topics in Chapter 6.
concepts.name_amharic: The concept of human right Human rights  (በአማርኛ)

concepts.name: State Action
concepts.deep_explanation: The rights set forth in Articles 2-21 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights include: freedom from discrimination; freedom from slavery; freedom from torture and from cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment; freedom from arbitrary arrest and detention; the right to a fair and public trial; freedom of thought, conscience, and religion; freedom of opinion and expression; and the right to participate in government through free elections

concepts.name: One Of The Distinguishing Features Of Th
concepts.simple_definition: One of the distinguishing features of the FDRE Constitution is the emphasis given to internationally recognized human rights norms
concepts.deep_explanation: This fundamental principle is stipulated in Article 10 of the constitution, which articulates, “Human rights and freedoms, emanating from the nature of mankind, are inviolable and inalienable”
